test: Compute on-hand at cut-off (running sum of WMS qty_delta) per SKU-branch, value at erp_products.unit_cost, compare with 2025 sales qty (WMS sale movements) to get months/years of supply. Break the >2-year excess value down by category, refrigerant (R-410A vs other), vendor type, branch, and value concentration. Check whether excess positions still received stock PO receipts in 2025, how long they have been excess (on-hand vs trailing-year sales at end of 2023/2024), and whether transfers drew from them. Size carrying cost on the excess above 2 years of supply (not the whole position) at an assumed rate.
support: Excess value is large (several $M) above a 2-year threshold, spread across many SKU-branches not only R-410A, persists across year-ends, and these positions keep getting stock receipts in 2025 while seldom supplying transfers.
weaken: Excess concentrated in R-410A equipment (regulatory phase-out, overlaps H3) or seasonal equipment; or excess positions receive no new stock POs (legacy stock just aging); or the excess quantity above 2 years is small in value once only the surplus portion is counted; or excess is an artefact of fractional opening balances / generated replenishment.
expect: Moderately confident (~60%) the excess exists at roughly the $10M position level, but I expect the surplus-above-two-years value to be smaller, a meaningful share tied to R-410A and to SKU-branches with no or tiny 2025 sales, and that replenishment POs are generated by a rule so excess positions may still get receipts. Carrying cost on the true surplus likely well under $2M/yr.
